Noida twin towers: why India's Supreme Court ordered two towers taller than Qutub Minar to be blown up.

Supertech's Apex and Ceyane stood in Emerald Court, Sector 93A, Noida. Nobody ever lived in them.

The case in short:
2009: a revised plan added two towers on the green area shown to earlier buyers.
2012: another revision took them from 24 to 40 floors.
The gap to an existing tower was about 9 m. The rules required 16 m.
Residents were not asked for consent, as the UP Apartments Act requires.
2014: Allahabad High Court ordered demolition.
31 Aug 2021: the Supreme Court upheld it, found collusion by Noida's planning authority, and ordered refunds to buyers with 12% a year interest.
28 Aug 2022: about 3,700 kg of explosives brought both towers down in seconds.

Was demolishing them the right call, or a waste? Send this to a friend buying a flat in NCR.

Sources: Supreme Court of India, Supertech Ltd v. Emerald Court Owner RWA (31 Aug 2021); Allahabad High Court (Apr 2014); demolition reports, 28 Aug 2022.

Ask to see all three before you pay any token money.

Why does Delhi have almost no skyscrapers? 🏙️

20 km away, Gurgaon and Noida are full of them. Delhi stayed low for three reasons:

1. Planes. Every building within 20 km of the airport needs a height clearance from the Airports Authority of India.
2. History. Delhi has 174 centrally protected monuments. Nothing new can be built within 100 m of them, and the next 200 m is regulated.
3. Lutyens' Delhi. The heart of the city is a bungalow zone, low-rise by design.

For years Delhi's tallest building was the Civic Centre, a government office at about 101 m. Noida's tallest, Cyberthum Tower A, is 213.7 m.

Then in August 2026, the Master Plan for Delhi 2047 removed height limits across most of the city, except areas like Lutyens' Delhi and near monuments.

Would you live on the 50th floor in Delhi? Comment YES or NO 👇

Sources: Height Restriction Rules 2015 (GSR 751(E)); ASI / AMASR Act; CTBUH; MPD 2047 (Aug 2026).

Six papers to see before a single rupee leaves your account for a plot.

1. Title deed and its chain, back about 30 years
2. A fresh encumbrance certificate
3. Jamabandi and mutation in the seller's name
4. Land-use change or conversion order
5. Approved layout and the RERA registration
6. Boundaries measured on the ground

Then have a property lawyer read all six. Record names differ by state.

Your brochure says 1,200 sq ft. Your tape measure says 800. Both are "correct".

Carpet area is the floor you can actually use, and it is the only one defined in law (Section 2(k), RERA Act). Built-up adds the walls and usually the balcony. Super built-up adds your share of the lobby, lifts and stairs. That extra share is called loading.

Before you book, ask for three things in writing: the carpet area, the loading percentage and the price per carpet sq ft.
